name: Ryan Pitylak
current_role: Executive Vice President of Growth, NinjaTrader (since May 2024); co-founder of ZenBusiness
profile: Austin-based marketer and entrepreneur (b. 1982) who co-founded ZenBusiness in 2015, a public-benefit corporation helping micro-businesses form and run companies, and served as its CMO; ZenBusiness reached a ~$1.7B valuation. In May 2024 he joined futures-trading platform NinjaTrader as EVP of Growth.
interesting_fact: Before ZenBusiness he co-founded and ran Unique Influence, a digital marketing firm acquired in 2015 by MDC Partners' media agency network Assembly.
deep_cut_fact: He earned undergraduate degrees in both economics and philosophy at the University of Texas.

public_contacts.value: https://ninjatrader.com/contact-us/ (has a Media & Communication Inquiries section)

notes: Wikipedia notes a 2004-06 spam-email history settled with Texas and Microsoft; avoid that topic. Now at NinjaTrader, so the ZenBusiness angle is past tense.

name: Yoni Tserruya
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lusha (Tel Aviv / New York)
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded Lusha with Assaf Eisenstein in 2016; the B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform grew largely bootstrapped before a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation. He still leads it as CEO, now pitching Lusha as a GTM data layer for AI agents via API and MCP.
interesting_fact: Lusha reached unicorn status in 2021 with a $205M Series B led by PSG at a $1.5B valuation after years of near-bootstrapped growth.
deep_cut_fact: Lusha began as a side project he built while working his first job as an iOS developer at AT&T, after studying computer science; he calls himself 'a builder at heart' who was 'more into tinkering than following plans'.
notes: Recent interview talks about AI agents and data infrastructure (MCP), a natural data/AI podcast angle.

name: Jiun Ee Teoh
current_role: Co-founder, CARSOME; CEO of CARSOME Academy
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur (known as 'JT') who co-founded CARSOME with Eric Cheng in 2015; it became Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform and Malaysia's first tech unicorn. A former COO and Chief Business Development Officer, he now runs CARSOME Academy, its accredited automotive training institution across Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
interesting_fact: CARSOME started in 2015 as an advertising platform and pivoted through trial and error to a used-car marketplace; the founders now preach that 'growth at all costs isn't a good mindset' after steering it to profitability.
deep_cut_fact: As CEO of CARSOME Academy he has spearheaded training partnerships with Sunway University, UniMAP, Beijing Business School, IUKL and Malaysia's MCMC; the academy has trained 1,500+ students and 6,500 corporate employees as automotive technicians.
notes: Eric Cheng is the public face of CARSOME; Teoh's background before CARSOME was in digital media.

name: Shay Filosof
current_role: Co-founder and Senior Software Engineer, Orca Security (Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli engineer and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (founded 2019), the agentless cloud-security company valued at $1.8B in 2021. Like several Orca founders he came from Check Point, where he was a software architect and R&D group manager; he remains at Orca in a hands-on engineering role building cloud-security products.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by a group of eight ex-Check Point engineers and executives, an unusually large founding team, and pioneered 'SideScanning' agentless cloud security.
deep_cut_fact: At Check Point he worked on firewall gateway performance as a software architect and R&D group manager; he holds a BSc in CS from the Academic College of Tel Aviv-Yaffo and an MSc in CS from the Open University of Israel.
notes: Very low public profile; details come mainly from directory profiles (TheOrg, Crunchbase). CEO Avi Shua / Gil Geron are Orca's public faces; approach via Orca's comms.

name: Zhaopeng Chen
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Agile Robots SE (Munich)
profile: Chinese-born roboticist who completed his doctorate at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and was deputy director of its Modular Dexterous Robotics Lab before co-founding Agile Robots with DLR scientist Peter Meusel in 2018. The Munich company makes force-sensitive AI-driven robot arms and systems and now the Agile ONE humanoid; it became a unicorn in 2021.
interesting_fact: At DLR he worked on the team that developed a widely acclaimed humanoid robotic hand, which became the basis of his first spin-off with Peter Meusel, Wessling Robotics, before Agile Robots.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong science-fiction fan, he says getting into his Chinese university's robotics institute 'was not easy'; from his third year he built robot hands and arms end-to-end, and at DLR spent years on robotic systems for outer space.
notes: No published press email found (site is JS-heavy); use the company website or DLR spin-off page (https://www.dlr.de/en/rm/transfer/spin-offs/agile-robots) for context. Space-robotics and humanoid angle fits a deep-tech podcast.

name: Mahesh Vellanki
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, SuperLayer (Web3 venture studio); co-founder of Forte and Rally (RLY) (current status unverified)
profile: Former Redpoint Ventures investor (Principal, 2012-18; earlier Citi investment banking) who co-founded blockchain-gaming platform Forte with Kevin Chou and others, which reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. With Chou he also co-founded the Rally/RLY social-token network and in 2021 the crypto venture studio SuperLayer.
interesting_fact: SuperLayer launched in Oct 2021 with backing from Marc Andreessen, Chris Dixon and Michael Ovitz, and in 2022 Polygon led a $25M fund for the studio.
deep_cut_fact: He moved from VC to founder: after six years as a Principal at Redpoint Ventures, he partnered with Kabam founder Kevin Chou; he studied finance at the University of Maryland's Robert H. Smith School of Business.
notes: No published contact found; low public profile since 2022. Rally/RLY wound down; confirm current focus before outreach. Education detail from directory profiles (MarketScreener/TheOrg).

name: Austin Allison
profile: Cincinnati-raised entrepreneur who founded real-estate transaction software dotloop in 2009, sold it to Zillow in 2015 (reported ~$108-120M) and ran it inside Zillow until 2018. He then co-founded Pacaso (2020), which sells co-owned second homes via property-specific LLCs; it hit a $1B valuation within five months, then a record for a US startup.
interesting_fact: Pacaso reached unicorn status in about five months after launch in 2020, among the fastest ever for a US startup.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a small town north of Cincinnati, the son of a carpenter, and says he was 'swinging a hammer starting at age three or four'; watching his father show up every day to provide shaped his work ethic.
notes: Frequent podcast guest and speaker; receptive to founder-story interviews.

name: Wang Anquan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Webull Corporation (Nasdaq: BULL)
profile: Chinese software engineer (Hunan University CS) who spent 2006-2012 at Alibaba's finance arm, then worked at Hengfeng Bank and as GM of Xiaomi Finance before founding Fumi Technology in 2016, parent of the Webull commission-free trading app. Webull listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in April 2025; he controls the majority of its voting power.
interesting_fact: Xiaomi, where he ran the finance business in 2015-16, was one of Fumi/Webull's early investors.
deep_cut_fact: Webull's first MVP was built in 2013 while he was still at Alibaba: he and an Ali colleague developed it as a market-intelligence tool, years before it became a brokerage.
notes: Very low Western media profile; Webull's US face is Anthony Denier. Best route is Webull IR/communications. Ownership/voting figures should be checked against 20-F.

name: Umesh Sachdev
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Uniphore (Palo Alto / Chennai)
profile: Indian-born tech entrepreneur who co-founded Uniphore with college friend Ravi Saraogi in 2008 in IIT Madras's rural-tech incubator, initially building multilingual speech recognition for rural Indian phone users. Uniphore became an enterprise conversational-AI and now 'business AI' platform valued at $2.5B in 2022, with backers incl. NVIDIA, AMD and Snowflake in a 2025 round.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he was the only Indian on TIME's list of 10 'Next Generation Leaders', for 'building a phone that can understand almost any language'.
deep_cut_fact: As Jaypee Institute (Noida) IT students in 2006, he and Saraogi first built a mobile-theft security product (Singularis Technologies, to track lost phones); it led IIT Madras professor Ashok Jhunjhunwala to invite them into IIT-M's Rural Technology and Business Incubator.

public_contacts.value: https://www.uniphore.com/author/usachdev/ (his author page on Uniphore blog)

notes: Also named MIT Tech Review Innovator Under 35 (India). AI/enterprise-data angle fits podcast; Uniphore's 2025 round included NVIDIA and AMD (verify specifics).

name: Jan Rubio
current_role: Co-founder and Principal Designer, Upside (formerly GetUpside), Washington DC (per investor/recruiting listings; current status unverified)
profile: Listed as a design-focused co-founder of Upside, the Washington DC cashback/rewards app founded in 2016 by CEO Alex Kinnier and others, which pays consumers cash back at gas stations, grocers and restaurants and was valued around $1.9-2B in 2021. Little else is publicly documented about Rubio.
interesting_fact: Upside's model gets merchants to fund consumer cashback only on incremental profit the app can prove it generated, an approach that took it to a ~$2B valuation within five years.
notes: Very low public profile; only roster mentions (MicroVentures, Welcome to the Jungle) as 'Designer & Co-Founder'. Identity details thin; CEO Alex Kinnier is the company's public face. Best route is via Upside comms.

name: James McCarthy
current_role: Co-founder of Flipdish (Dublin); commercial lead (listed variously as COO, CCO and CRO)
profile: Irish entrepreneur who co-founded Flipdish in 2015 with his brother, CEO Conor McCarthy. Flipdish gives restaurants and takeaways their own branded online-ordering apps, kiosks and POS as an alternative to commission-heavy marketplaces; it became an Irish unicorn in 2022 at a $1.25B valuation after a ~$100M raise led by Tiger Global.
interesting_fact: Flipdish hit unicorn status in Jan 2022 at a $1.25B valuation, raising c.$100M to expand globally as hospitality digitised during the pandemic.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as an architect, he came up with The Christmas Shirt Company in 2011 while working at an architecture firm in Dublin during the recession, pitching Christmas shirts as a cooler alternative to the Christmas jumper and selling via Shopify.
notes: Conor McCarthy is the public face/CEO. The architect/Christmas-shirt link to the Flipdish co-founder comes via Conor's Business & Finance interview (https://businessandfinance.com/news/there-are-1000s-of-ways-to-achieve-something-and-no-single-correct-way-of-doing-anything-ceo-qa-with-conor-mccarthy-ceo-cto-of-flipdish/); double-check before use.

name: Smita Deorah
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, LEAD Group (LEAD School), Mumbai
profile: Former Procter & Gamble finance/treasury/strategy leader (nine years in Singapore and India) who co-founded LEAD with Sumeet Mehta in 2012. LEAD provides an integrated curriculum, teacher training and tech system to affordable private schools in India's small towns; it reached a $1.1B valuation in Jan 2022 after a $100M Series E.
interesting_fact: LEAD began in 2012 as a single school on the outskirts of Ahmedabad with 14 students and grew into a system serving thousands of affordable private schools across India.
deep_cut_fact: Before LEAD, she and Sumeet Mehta started Sparsh, an NGO for Mumbai's Anganwadis, implementing a 'pre-school in a box' in 16 Anganwadi centres to prepare children for school and reduce dropouts.
notes: Regular speaker (ASU+GSV Summit 'Power of Women' honoree, DNA Changemaker in Education 2024). No published press email found.

name: Carlos Paniagua
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Glia (based in Tartu, Estonia)
profile: Guatemala-born software engineer who co-founded Glia with Dan Michaeli and Justin DiPietro; Glia's digital customer-service platform (voice, chat, video, co-browsing and AI) is used mainly by banks and credit unions. He built its engineering hub in Tartu, and Glia became Estonia's tenth unicorn in 2021.
interesting_fact: Although Glia is headquartered in New York, Paniagua proposed moving the developer team to Tartu, recruiting engineers he had studied with, making Glia counted as an Estonian unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Originally from Guatemala, he moved to Estonia in 2010 on a scholarship to study a master's in software engineering at the University of Tartu; he advises foreign founders there to learn Estonian ('It's very powerful').
notes: Active in Estonian startup community (LIFT99, Startup Day). CEO Dan Michaeli is Glia's public face in the US. No published press email found.

name: Stephen Hawthornthwaite
current_role: Co-founder and Chair of the Board, Rothy's (CEO until Jan 2024)
profile: Former tech M&A banker (GCA Savvian, InfoSpace corporate development) who co-founded San Francisco shoe brand Rothy's with Roth Martin in 2012 (launched 2016), known for flats knit from recycled plastic bottles. He was CEO until January 2024, when Jenny Ming took over and he became board chair; Brazil's Alpargatas bought a 49.9% stake at a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Rothy's built its own vertically integrated factory in Dongguan, China, the world's first shoe manufacturer to earn both LEED and TRUE Platinum certification, and has diverted 166M+ plastic bottles from landfill.
deep_cut_fact: On a 2020 Talks at GS episode he said the founding bet was that 'fashionable products aren't always comfortable... and sustainable products historically haven't been made with the quality and attention to detail they deserve', so Rothy's set out to do all three at once.

public_contacts.value: adore@rothys.com (Anna Doré, Senior Director of Communications, as of Jan 2024)

notes: Spent ~20 years in M&A/investment banking before Rothy's (directory profiles also list Duke undergrad and Wake Forest law degree; unverified). Press contact is from a Jan 2024 release; may be stale.

name: Umang Rustagi
current_role: Co-founder and President Director, Kredivo (Indonesia); Deputy CEO of Kredivo Group (formerly FinAccel)
profile: Indian-born former McKinsey financial-services consultant (IIM Bangalore MBA) who co-founded FinAccel in 2015 with Akshay Garg and Alie Tan. Its Kredivo app pioneered digital 'buy now, pay later' credit lines in Indonesia, turning phones into credit cards for the underbanked; the group, valued around $2B, also owns Krom Bank and operates in Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand.
interesting_fact: Kredivo was built to give Indonesians without credit cards an instant digital credit line at checkout; Google highlighted FinAccel as 'turning mobile phones into credit cards'.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding FinAccel he worked in McKinsey's financial-services practice; the founding team was pitched to recruits as 'Akshay Garg (cofounder Komli Media), Umang Rustagi (McKinsey financial services) and Alie Tan (PicStory and Affle)'.
notes: Runs the Indonesian operating business from Jakarta; Group CEO Akshay Garg is the main public spokesperson. Kredivo's 2022 SPAC deal with VPC Impact Acquisition Holdings II was terminated.

name: Brooke Partelow
current_role: Listed as co-founder of MNTN (formerly SteelHouse); current role unknown
profile: Named in aggregator profiles as co-founder, with CEO Mark Douglas, of SteelHouse (2009), a retargeting ad-tech firm that pivoted to self-serve connected-TV advertising and rebranded as MNTN in 2021; MNTN, whose Chief Creative Officer is Ryan Reynolds, listed on the NYSE in May 2025. No biographical information on Partelow could be verified.
interesting_fact: MNTN owns Ryan Reynolds' creative agency Maximum Effort, and Reynolds serves as its Chief Creative Officer.
notes: Essentially no public footprint under this name (searches return nothing; not named in SEC full-text search). Founding claim comes from a single aggregator (yespress.io/mntn.md). Treat identity as unconfirmed; route via MNTN comms if needed.

name: Todd Southwick
current_role: Co-founder of iTrustCapital (CEO through ~2022; current title unverified)
profile: Southern California entrepreneur who co-founded iTrustCapital in 2018 with Blake Skadron, a software platform letting investors buy and trade crypto and physical gold/silver inside tax-advantaged self-directed IRAs. After bootstrapping for three years, it raised a $125M Series A in early 2022 at a $1.3B post-money valuation. Kevin Maloney is listed as CEO in later sources.
interesting_fact: iTrustCapital bootstrapped to unicorn: it raised no outside capital for three years before its $125M Series A at a $1.3B valuation, growing largely via crypto YouTuber promotion and word of mouth.
deep_cut_fact: In mid-2022 he wrote an essay titled 'The Most Boring Company in Crypto', arguing 'We choose to be boring, pragmatic, and responsible... a little bit of boring goes a long way.'
notes: Low public profile since 2022; confirm his current role before outreach. No published press email found. Co-founder Blake Skadron has been more visible in LA Business Journal coverage.

name: Tomas Okmanas
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Nord Security (NordVPN); co-founder of Tesonet and nexos.ai
profile: Vilnius-born entrepreneur (b. 1987, also known as Tom Okman) who co-founded venture builder Tesonet with Eimantas Sabaliauskas in 2008 and NordVPN in 2012; Nord Security (NordVPN, NordPass, NordLayer) was valued at $3B in 2023. Tesonet also helped build Oxylabs, Hostinger and Surfshark. In 2025 he launched enterprise AI platform nexos.ai, which raised a $35M Series A at a $350M valuation.
interesting_fact: He says the idea for nexos.ai came to him on 28 Oct 2024 and the product was ready in 30 days; he also bought basketball club London Lions in 2024 and is a part-owner of EuroLeague's Zalgiris.
deep_cut_fact: He studied history (BA, Vilnius University) and is a named inventor on a US patent for a NordVPN method that cuts the time TCP packets take between client, VPN server and destination; Tesonet tried 34 projects, from computer games to web hosting, before finding its focus.
notes: Named National Patron of Lithuania with Sabaliauskas for Ukraine fundraising. Strong AI/infrastructure angle via nexos.ai. Wikipedia lists him as 'Tom Okman' redirect.

name: Brett Goldberg
profile: Lehigh finance grad (2007) and ex-Barclays investment banker who co-founded TickPick in 2011 with college roommate Chris O'Brien. TickPick is a no-buyer-fee secondary ticket marketplace that bootstrapped for years before its first institutional round ($40M, 2019) and was later valued around $1B; he remains co-CEO.
interesting_fact: TickPick launched in 2012 as an eBay-style ticket bidding platform; when users asked 'How do I just buy tickets?', the founders pivoted to pricing and eliminated buyer service fees, now its signature.
deep_cut_fact: He chose Lehigh to compete in Division I track and field; the TickPick idea came from buying and reselling tickets to multiple Red Hot Chili Peppers concerts, and he would scrape StubHub listings into Excel to price them.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Mixergy, Sports Tao, The Route); writes for Entrepreneur.com. Good founder-story candidate.
